Chapter 2  Nutrition Assessment for Nurse Practitioners   19
Vital Signs and Anthropometric Measures
Documents that report comprehensive encounters must contain the appropriate set 
of vital signs. In the adult, vital signs include blood pressure, heart rate, respiration 
rate, temperature, height, weight, and body mass index (BMI). It is also helpful to 
obtain a waist circumference. Additional documentation is often used in the pediatric 
setting to track height, weight, growth, and development.
